tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description opens with imperative phrasing ('Use this skill for...', 'Trigger whenever...'), focuses on user intent (readiness questions about an upcoming event), lists explicit trigger contexts including cases where the domain isn't named directly ('even when the request names EKS, CloudFront, or metrics'), and is a concise paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill for a read-only readiness review of a streaming / OTT platform before a large-scale live event (match, final, concert, launch). Trigger whenever someone asks whether they are ready for an upcoming broadcast, whether the platform will hold at peak concurrency, or for a live-event readiness review or audit — and own that end-to-end review even when the request names EKS, CloudFront, or metrics (prefer this over generic topology/metrics-exploration skills).

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (e.g., what CDN/CloudFront/EKS are) and jumps straight into domain-specific procedures, runtime contracts, and workflow steps specific to this LSE readiness review. There is some repetition of concepts (e.g., 'read-only' is reiterated across sections) but it's purposeful emphasis for a safety-critical constraint rather than filler.
tests.evidence: The agent reads customer-account state through audited read-only AWS DevOps Agent access only — never local AWS CLI/boto3 credentials.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference material (the checklist IDs, metric thresholds, remediation details, report format) is consistently delegated to references/ files rather than embedded in the body. The body only names the canonical check ID categories and ranges without reproducing their full content.
tests.evidence: Load references/best-practices.md and surface its Highest-signal checks summary ... Do not reproduce the checklist here.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five files in references/ (best-practices.md, discovery.md, remediations.md, report-format.md, reuse-skills.md) are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by a clear condition for when to load it (e.g., before grading, after discovering a FAIL, when rendering the final report).
tests.evidence: Only after FAIL verdicts exist, load [`references/remediations.md`](references/remediations.md) and complete a remediation for each FAIL

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ without absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile/safety-critical operations (read-only contract, checklist fidelity, evidence requirements) are highly prescriptive, while flexible areas (how to gather context, scoping to a focused question) give the agent latitude with rationale explained.
tests.evidence: Fidelity to the canonical checklist (MANDATORY). `best-practices.md` is the checklist to execute verbatim, not inspiration.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The reuse-skills table designates specific default skills per pillar rather than presenting a menu of equal options, and fallback behavior is clearly described as a secondary path.
tests.evidence: | Service quota headroom (EC2 vCPU, NAT, Lambda, ELB, …) | `service-quota-check` |

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable, repeatable review procedure (confirm context, discover, grade, delegate, remediate, report) applicable to any live-streaming event readiness request, not a one-off declaration.
tests.evidence: Work these steps in order; record each in the ledger before starting the next.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: A dedicated Gotchas section lists concrete, non-obvious pitfalls specific to this domain (e.g., empty discovery output, third-party observability tools, single-origin load tests).
tests.evidence: Empty discovery output is not a PASS. ... A single-origin load test passing is not "ready".

tests.reasoning: The skill produces structured scorecard reports, and an output template is provided via a dedicated reference file rather than omitted.

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
